items.title: Despite concerns, AI becomes daily fixture in physician workflows
items.excerpt: A Doximity survey of 3,300+ U.S. physicians finds the share using AI for clinical decision support nearly doubled to 63% (from 37% in 2025); nearly half worry about overreliance and skill erosion. (Same survey covered by AuntMinnie: 64% of radiologists use AI daily.)
items.rationale: Freshest item (11-12): a 3,300-physician survey showing clinical-decision-support AI use nearly doubled to 63%, with skill-erosion worries — a clinician-facing snapshot of everyday practice.

items.title: New documents raise more questions about Medicare's AI prior-authorization experiment
items.excerpt: STAT Health Tech reports newly surfaced documents raising further questions about CMS's WISeR model, the Medicare experiment that uses AI vendors to run prior authorization on selected services.
items.rationale: Insurance-review automation hitting Medicare patients: newly surfaced CMS documents on the WISeR AI prior-auth pilot, a different event from the 10-30 JAMA utilization study.

items.title: FDA, CMS look to collaborate with states on health AI
items.excerpt: Federal officials at FDA and CMS signal they want to work with states on regulating health AI, alongside a push to protect doctors from AI-related liability.
items.rationale: Regulator-facing: FDA and CMS signal federal-state coordination on health-AI oversight plus physician liability protection; earlier state-lobbying and AMA liability cards covered other actors.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Use in Interventional Clinical Trials Registered on ClinicalTrials.gov
items.excerpt: Cross-sectional study of how artificial intelligence is being used in interventional clinical trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov since 2022. (Date: Crossref created.)
items.rationale: Primary peer-reviewed source mapping where AI is actually being tested in interventional trials, a view of the clinical evidence pipeline that no earlier card has covered.

items.title: Predicting persistent fever in patients with cancer receiving antibiotics: a machine learning approach
items.excerpt: ML models built on EHR data from two academic hospitals predict which hospitalized cancer patients will remain febrile 48–72 h after starting IV antibiotics, externally validated, to curb extra imaging and antimicrobial escalation.
items.rationale: Bedside oncology/infectious-disease decision support with external validation, aimed at avoiding unnecessary imaging and antibiotic escalation; it is a disease-specific clinical model, not the 10-20 opioid EHR card.

dedup.note: Pool of 10, none removed as a near-verbatim repeat. WISeR (STAT 11-12) is tagged 'related' to the 10-30 JAMA WISeR utilization study, but it reports a different event (newly surfaced CMS documents), so it is kept as new and that study is named as nearest. Not picked: STAT 'doctors consult chatbots' (STAT is already at the 2-per-outlet cap, and it is analysis close to the 10-16 OpenEvidence and 10-26 Doximity Ask cards). WIRED Gemini teen-suicide lawsuit (the candidate note flags possible politics/gadgets overlap, and published_urls.json was too large to grep across sections without Bash, so skipped to avoid a cross-section duplicate). Radiology Business AI inflammation score (related to the 10-27 coronary-inflammation card, and cardiology is saturated). RETBind retinal foundation model (leans science; no clinical deployment). Science bioadhesive (AI is only incidental, and the body could not be fetched). Cross-section exact-grep of published_urls.json for the 5 picks was not possible in this toolset (file is 4,342 lines; only the books section was read).
